<thought>Based on the monoisotopic mass (≈183.045 Da) the molecular formula is C9H10ClNO. The 13C NMR shows a carbonyl carbon at ~169 ppm and aromatic carbons (6 signals between 123–133 ppm), plus two aliphatic carbons (~43 and 26 ppm). Among the isomers for C9H10ClNO, the structure **CC(=O)C1=CC(=C(C=C1)N)CCl** (4‑chloro‑2‑aminobenzoyl‑methyl, i.e., a chloro‑anilide with an acetyl group) matches these features: it has a carbonyl (amide/ketone) giving the 169 ppm signal, an aromatic ring with chlorine and an amino substituent accounting for the aromatic carbon shifts, and a methyl carbon (≈26 ppm) and a carbonyl‑adjacent carbon (≈43 ppm). The SMILES is valid and consistent with all observed data.> 
<final_answer>CC(=O)C1=CC(=C(C=C1)N)CCl</final_answer>
